This time, the resulting limit still gives the indeterminate form 00. To find the limit, we apply L'Hopital's rule once again. We get limx→−43(x+4)2(x+5)−2/3−1=limx→−4[3(x+4)2]′[(x+5)−2/3−1]′=limx→−46(x+4)−23(x+5)−5/3=−9limx→−4(x+4)(x+5)5/3=−9(−4+4)(−4+5)5/3=−9⋅0⋅1=0.

KP 3. Calculating an Indeterminate Limit of the Form Infinity Divided by Infinity Using L'Hopital's Rule
5.?

Evaluate limx→0+cot⁡2xcot⁡x.

H
Tue, Aug 18th @ 5:26 PM|Elapsed: 11:09Correct

Here the limits of the numerator and denominator are limx→0+cot⁡2x=∞ and limx→0+cot⁡x=∞, respectively, so we have the case ∞∞.

Applying L'Hopital's rule, we obtain

limx→0+cot⁡2xcot⁡x=limx→0+[cot⁡2x]′[cot⁡x]′=limx→0+(−2csc2⁡2x)−csc2⁡x=limx→0+2⋅(1sin2⁡2x)(1sin2⁡x)=limx→0+2sin2⁡xsin2⁡2x=limx→0+2sin2⁡x(2sin⁡xcos⁡x)2=limx→0+2sin2⁡x4sin2⁡xcos2⁡x=limx→0+2sin2⁡x4sin2⁡xcos2⁡x=limx→0+12cos2⁡x=12cos2⁡0=12.

6.?

Evaluate limx→π2−ln⁡(cos⁡x)tan⁡x.

Tue, Aug 18th @ 5:41 PM|Elapsed: 14:44Correct

Here the limits of the numerator and denominator are limx→π2−ln⁡(cos⁡x)=−∞ and limx→π2−tan⁡x=∞, respectively, so we have the case −∞∞.

Applying L'Hopital's rule, we obtain

limx→π2−ln⁡(cos⁡x)tan⁡x=limx→π2−[ln⁡(cos⁡x)]′[tan⁡x]′=limx→π2−(−sin⁡xcos⁡x)sec2⁡x=−limx→π2−(sin⁡xcos⁡x)(1cos2⁡x)=−limx→π2−sin⁡xcos2⁡xcos⁡x=−limx→π2−sin⁡xcos⁡x=−sin⁡(π2)cos⁡(π2)=0.

7.?

Evaluate limx→∞ln2⁡xx.

M
Tue, Aug 18th @ 10:55 PM|Elapsed: 3:19Correct

Here the limits of the numerator and denominator are limx→∞ln2⁡x=∞ and limx→∞x=∞, respectively, so we have the case ∞∞.

Applying L'Hopital's rule, we obtain

limx→∞ln2⁡xx=limx→∞[ln2⁡x]′[x]′=limx→∞(2ln⁡xx)1=−limx→∞2ln⁡xx.

This time, the resulting limit still gives the indeterminate form ∞∞. To find the limit, we apply L'Hopital's rule once again. We get limx→∞(ln⁡x)2x=limx→∞2ln⁡xx=limx→∞[2ln⁡x]′[x]′=limx→∞(2x)1=2limx→∞1x=0.

In this case, we have an indeterminate form of type ∞∞, so applying L'Hopital's rule yields

limx→∞x+1x−1=limx→∞[x+1]′[x−1]′=limx→∞1(12x)=limx→∞2x=∞.
